user.t:
Web research (read-only; no installs; no files except your answer). Date-stamp: 2026-10-11. Product context: scoup.ai is a freight-cost recovery platform (detects unpaid/underbilled truck detention, invoice overcharges like unauthorized accessorials, rate/fuel mismatches, duplicates; builds evidence packets; four-eyes approval; contingency pricing idea). Research the CUSTOMERS with real, cited numbers (grade each source: A gov/peer-reviewed/large survey with method, B industry study with method, C vendor/anecdote):
1. US trucking carriers: number of for-hire carriers by fleet size (FMCSA/ATA), revenue per truck, operating cost per mile and its components (ATRI Operational Costs of Trucking 2024/2025: fuel, driver wages, insurance, tolls...), operating margins/ratios, how much detention/accessorial leakage costs them, factoring usage and fees, what software they use (TMS, ELD), willingness to pay, top pains (surveys: ATRI Top Industry Issues 2025, OOIDA).
2. Freight brokers / 3PLs: count, gross margins (TIA data), accessorial collection pain, payment terms, claims workload.
3. Shippers (manufacturers, retailers, CPG, importers): freight spend as % of revenue (CSCMP State of Logistics 2025: US business logistics costs, transport share), freight audit & payment usage, inbound accessorial disputes, container demurrage & detention exposure for importers.
4. Europe/Norway briefly (Standgeld HGB §412; market size), since the founder is Norwegian.
5. Competitor/adjacent pricing: freight audit firms (fee % of spend or per invoice), detention apps (DockClock etc.), Loop, Cass, factoring (rates %), DAT/Truckstop subscriptions — public price points.
6. Synthesize: 3 customer segments ranked by (pain $ per account per year, ability to pay, reachability, data access), with the 5 most valuable jobs-to-be-done per segment and which ones scoup can serve with its current engine vs new features.
Return a compact report (tables, every number with URL + grade, ~1200 words). Flag weak evidence explicitly.

handback.t:
## scoup.ai customer research (as of 2026-10-11)

I ran web searches only. I installed nothing and wrote no files.

**Grades:** A = government, peer-reviewed or large survey with a stated method. B = industry study with a method. C = vendor material, aggregator or anecdote.

**Caveat:** Many numbers come from trade-press write-ups of the primary report, not the report itself. I note this where it matters. Before anything goes in front of investors, pull the primary PDFs, especially the ATRI ones.

### 1. US trucking carriers

| Metric | Value | Source | Grade |
|---|---|---|---|
| Carriers with operating authority | 339,220 in 2024 (down 3.7% from 2023); roughly flat in 2025 | [Trucking Dive, FMCSA data](https://www.truckingdive.com/news/fmcsa-grants-reinstatements-revocations-operating-authority-2025-data/808968/) | B |
| Fleet size | 91.3% run 6 or fewer trucks; 97.4% run fewer than 20 | [ATA/FMCSA via ai-analytics](https://ai-analytics.org/writing/fmcsa-carriers/) | B (secondhand) |
| Industry revenue | $906B in 2024; 76.9% of freight revenue | [ATA Trends via SC247](https://www.supplychain247.com/article/truck-volumes-ebound-2025-ata-freight-forecast/news) | B |
| Operating cost (2025) | $2.336/mile, a record. Fuel $0.482. Driver wages $0.818 + benefits $0.210. Tolls +13.2%, repair and maintenance +8.6% | [TT News](https://www.ttnews.com/articles/atri-truck-costs-2025), [FleetOwner](https://www.fleetowner.com/operations/article/55392569/atri-report-breaks-down-class-8-truck-operating-costs-by-region-and-expense-category) | A/B (ATRI survey of fleets) |
| Insurance premium | $0.099/mile (2023 data, +12.5%) | [ATRI 2024](https://truckingresearch.org/2024/06/new-atri-research-industry-costs-increased-more-than-6-percent-during-freight-recession/) | A/B |
| Margins | Truckload: −2.3% operating margin in 2024, +0.4% in 2025. Every sector except LTL was at or below 6% (2023 data) | [TLI](https://tlimagazine.com/news/new-atri-report-indicates-fleet-profit-margins-fall-amid-rising-costs/), [ATRI 2024](https://truckingresearch.org/2024/06/new-atri-research-industry-costs-increased-more-than-6-percent-during-freight-recession/) | A/B |
| Detention leakage (2023 data) | $3.6B direct cost plus $11.5B lost productivity. Drivers detained at 39.3% of stops. 94.5% of fleets bill detention but are paid on fewer than 50% of those invoices. Average fee $63.71/hr, usually starting after 2 hours free time | [ATRI 2024](https://truckingresearch.org/2024/09/new-research-documents-substantial-financial-and-safety-impacts-from-truck-driver-detention/), [Fleet Equipment](https://www.fleetequipmentmag.com/atri-driver-detention-impacts/) | A/B |
| Owner-operator detention | 14.3 hrs/week detained. Only 29% are paid on all loads. Those who claim are paid on about 25% of detained loads | [OOIDA Foundation](https://landline.media/ooida-foundation-releases-freight-rate-detention-time-survey-results/) | B (self-selected members; older survey) |
| Factoring fees | 1–5% per invoice. Recourse about 1–3%, non-recourse 3–7%. Solo operators under $25k/month pay 3–5% | [FreightWaves](https://www.freightwaves.com/news/freight-factoring-rates-how-much-does-factoring-really-cost), [otrucking](https://otrucking.com/resources/guides/freight-factoring-rates-2026/) | C |
| Factoring use | Of 350+ surveyed carriers 
[...]
(https://www.supplychain247.com/paper/the_davis_logistics_cost_and_service_database) | B (old vintage) |
| Recoverable through audit | Invoice error rate 3–8%. Recovery 2–5% (claims up to 10%) of spend | [amzprep](https://amzprep.com/freight-bill-audit-payment/), [beancount](https://beancount.io/blog/2026/09/21/freight-invoice-audit-recover-overcharges-duplicate-charges-guide) | **C, weak. Vendor marketing; do not quote externally.** |
| Container demurrage and detention | 9 ocean carriers collected about $15.4B (Apr 2020 to Mar 2025), about $3B/yr. Q4 2024 was 85% above Q2 2020. New FMC billing rules took effect May 2024 | [FMC](https://www.fmc.gov/detention-and-demurrage/), [HFW](https://www.hfw.com/insights/fmcs-new-demurrage-and-detention-regulations-become-effective-may-2024) | A |

### 4. Europe and Norway

| Metric | Value | Source | Grade |
|---|---|---|---|
| EU road freight volume | 1,869bn tonne-km in 2024 (+0.6%). Poland 20%, Germany 15% | [Eurostat](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php/Road_freight_transport_statistics) | A |
| European road freight market | €424bn (2023), about €431bn forecast for 2024 | [Ti Insight](https://ti-insight.com/press_releases/european-road-freight-market-to-return-to-growth-in-2024-and-expand-by-1-6/) | B |
| Norway volume | Norwegian trucks: 24.1bn tonne-km and 259.4M tonnes in 2024 | [SSB](https://www.ssb.no/transport-og-reiseliv/landtransport/statistikk/godstransport-med-lastebil/artikler) | A |
| Norway market size | Production about NOK 61bn (2023) | [ReportLinker](https://www.reportlinker.com/dataset/cd9dd0883f17b1b6592567d7f30fdd5375d623d2) | C |
| Germany: waiting-time pay (Standgeld) | HGB §412(3) gives carriers a statutory right to "reasonable" pay for waiting beyond loading/unloading time. The Federal Court of Justice (BGH, I ZR 37/09) ruled that standard terms excluding it are invalid. About €60/hr is reported as accepted by the courts | [rewis §412](https://rewis.io/gesetze/hgb/p/hgb-412/), [BGH](https://gesetze.co/urteile/I_ZR_37-09), [VerkehrsRundschau](https://www.verkehrsrundschau.de/nachrichten/recht-geld/urteil-standgeld-bei-ueberziehung-des-ladezeitfensters-rechtens-2993240) | A for the statute and ruling; C for the €60 |

**Gap:** I did not verify any Norwegian equivalent, whether in the domestic road freight act (vegfraktloven) or the CMR convention. Do not claim one yet.

### 5. Competitor and adjacent pricing

| Player | Public price point | Grade |
|---|---|---|
| Freight audit (contingency) | 20–50% of what is recovered ([beancount](https://beancount.io/blog/2026/09/21/freight-invoice-audit-recover-overcharges-duplicate-charges-guide)) | C |
| Cass | Per-invoice fee, custom quote. About $90B paid per year, 50M invoices, $130M fee revenue (TTM) ([Cass investor presentation](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/708781/000070878124000035/investorpresentationq120.htm)). That implies roughly **$2.60 of fee revenue per invoice**, which is my calculation | A for filing figures |
| Loop | Enterprise only, no public pricing. About $44M annualized revenue (Mar 2026); merged with Data2Logistics Aug 2025 ([Sacra](https://sacra.com/c/loop)) | C |
| DockClock (Platform Science) | Uses ELD data to bill detention automatically. No public price ([marketplace](https://www.platformscience.com/marketplace/dockclock)) | C |
| DAT One | $54–339 per user per month ([otrucking](https://otrucking.com/resources/guides/dat-load-board-pricing-plans/)) | C |
| Factoring | 1–5% of invoice (see section 1) | C |

Truckstop pricing: not found.

### 6. Synthesis: three segments, ranked

Ranked on pain $ per account, ability to pay, reachability and data access.

**1. Mid-market US shippers and importers ($10–100M freight spend).**
- *Pain:* about 2–5% of spend (weak C evidence), roughly $0.2–5M per account. Importers add demurrage/detention exposure on top.
- *Ability to pay:* high; contingency pricing is already the norm.
- *Data access:* good (AP/ERP, EDI 210 invoices, rate contracts).
- *Reachability:* medium. Long sales cycles; Cass, Loop and many audit firms compete here.
- *Top jobs:*
  1. Catch overcharges and unauthorized extra charges (accessorials) — **current engine**
  2. Catch rate and fuel-surcharge mismatches against contract — **current engine**
  3. Catch duplicate bills — **current engine**
  4. Dispute carrier detention claims using appointment/dock data — **partial** (evidence packets exist; needs dock-scheduling integration)
  5. Audit container demurrage/detention against the FMC May-2024 billing rules — **new feature**

**2. Mid-size brokers and 3PLs.**
- *Pain:* margins near 15% and squeezed; they absorb detention when they cannot re-bill the shipper (inferred, unquantified).
- *Ability to pay:* medium. *Data access:* TMS plus rate confirmations. *Reachability:* good (~28k firms, TIA channel).
- *Top jobs:*
  1. Audit carrier invoices against rate confirmations — **current engine**
  2. Detect duplicates — **current engine**
  3. Re-bill accessorials to shippers with an evidence packet — **current engine** (evidence packets + four-eyes approval)
  4. Automate the claims workflow — **new feature**
  5. Pull ELD/geofence proof of arrival and departure — **new feature**

**3. Small and mid carriers (10–100 trucks).**
- *Pain:* detention, billed at about $64/hr and collected on fewer than half of invoices.
- *Illustrative, my assumption:* 1–2 billable detention hours per truck per week ≈ $3–6k/truck/yr uncollected. That is about $30–600k per account, but margins are near zero.
- *Ability to pay:* low. A recovery-share or factoring-linked model fits better than SaaS.
- *Reachability:* high but fragmented; 91% of carriers run 6 or fewer trucks and are probably too small.
- *Data access:* ELDs are universal; integration is needed.
- *Top jobs:*
  1. Detect unbilled detention — **current engine**
  2. Build a claim packet with timestamps — **current engine**
  3. Pull ELD timestamps automatically — **new feature**
  4. Chase collection — **new feature**
  5. Push to factor or invoice — **new feature**

**Overall:** lead with shippers, or brokers for a faster sales cycle. Treat carriers as a channel play through factoring companies or ELD marketplaces rather than direct sales.

### Weakest evidence, flagged
- The shipper recovery rate (2–5%) and the contingency fee range (20–50%) come from vendor marketing.
- Small-carrier willingness to pay and TMS adoption: no data.
- Broker accessorial losses: no data.
- The Norwegian waiting-time rule is unverified.
- The 2026 State of Logistics figures are secondhand.
- Per-account dollar figures in section 6 are my estimates.
